This revision (v9) answers the v8 review's four objections: (1) the unit convention is the organiser's own normalisation clause - COST_MODEL.md states the prices are 'rounded organizer normalization constants ... not CPU timings or exact measured instruction counts' and sets candidate_prices_allowed: false (a reference operation costs one group-equivalent unit), so non-group work is charged as actual itemised instructions divided by the pinned 2000-instruction reference budget, never re-priced at a cheaper measured mul; (2) the point scalar multiplication is charged at 648 reference additions - the 4-bit fixed-window Jacobian itemisation (2874 F_r-multiplications = 1,100,742 instructions, non-mul field work 49,500, window indexing 504, final affine conversion 1149 plus one 65,536-instruction inversion) NOW INCLUDING the 15-entry window table's affine normalisation by one batched inversion ((2*15-1)M + inv = 76,660 instructions), total 1,295,091 instructions = 647.5 reference additions; (3) C1 is the bounded-increment Bernstein inequality (each giant lookup contributes one head-slot occupancy, an increment in [0, 64] - the C2 cap - with variance bound 64 mu) evaluated at the WORST mean inside the C3 envelope, and C3 prices only the envelope's breach, its cost being carried inside C1; (4) H1 gains exact-coverage support: a twelve-prime census enumerates the covered set C = {b*u/g} exactly on asymptotic-shaped toy structures at the claim's own K and matches the diagonal-corrected law within +-0.0067 with deviations of both signs.

heuristics: H1 (coverage; the load-bearing heuristic): the 6N^2(1 - (L-1)/L^2) independent rationals a w/(u a' w') hit z = s^d like uniform elements of the order-m subgroup H, so the success probability is at least 1 - e^{-K} = 0.39195 at the lower bound K = 0.4975 (the realised 6N^2/m is 0.4975 x (1 + 2^-51), N = 64392490294377459008906942102896640 = 2^64 x L exactly). Support: Lemma 4 (the six-fold symmetry and the parity key make the six orbit images of one record share one key and one comparison), the L-entry walk list giving exactly N = 2^64 x L distinct scalars per side, the diagonal collapse K' = K(1 - (L-1)/L^2), the three coverage toys (d = 32/64/128 at r ~ 2^27.6/2^29.7/2^31.7, measured 0.4167/0.4333/0.3333 against predicted 0.3974/0.3913/0.3974, z = +0.43/+0.94/-1.43), NEW the exact-coverage census (twelve genuine primes with 6d | r-1, semiprime baby/giant sets sized at the claim's K over one shared walk list, the covered set C = {b*u/g mod r_t} enumerated EXACTLY: mean absolute deviation 0.0032 from the diagonal-corrected law, worst 0.0067, deviations of both signs - 8 positive, 4 negative), and the end-to-end toy (measured 0.3833 against 0.3935 predicted, z = -0.23).

H2 and H2' (supply): a fraction 1/2^20 of primes near q are H-primes (q^m = 1 mod r); gaps between consecutive H-primes are exponential with mean 2^20 ln q, so the L-th (L = 2^51.6387) H-prime above 2^39 is below 2^78 and a gap above 2^33 among the listed ones has probability < 2^-167 per list (such gaps split into two table entries against the reserve). The base-prime search interval [2^80, F] is sized by the fixed point X = 2^66*2^20*ln(F) (X ~ 2^92.0), so the integrand bound 1/ln(q) >= 1/ln(F) gives an expected supply of at least 2^66 against the 2^65 requirement, the shortfall the Chernoff tail C9 under H2'' (independent membership indicators). Checked by the run's H-prime sanity block: 402 of the 6542 primes below 2^16 are sixteenth powers against 408.875 expected (binomial z = -0.34).

H3 (key bits): the 192-bit parity-selected y keys of the walked points behave like independent uniform strings across the six-element mu_6 orbits. This is a heuristic about coordinates of structured points; the end-to-end toy bins 16-bit truncated keys into 32 pseudo-nodes x 16 heads and reports occupancy chi^2 = 24.27 on 31 degrees of freedom (z = -0.85).

Caps C1-C9 (ours, every tail rounded towards the larger probability): C1 comparisons per node - Bernstein for bounded increments, each giant lookup contributing one head-slot occupancy in [0, 64] (the C2 cap) with variance bound 64 mu, evaluated at the C3-envelope worst mean mu x (1 + 2^-9) against the 1.01 x mu cap: per-node tail 2^-937.2, over all 2^84 nodes 2^-853.2; C2 head-slot depth (Poisson 0.389, tail 2^-82.6 over 2^117 slots); C3 node record-count deviations (Chernoff 2^-2969.5 over all nodes; the deviation's cost is carried inside C1, which is evaluated at the envelope's worst mean); C4 false candidate pairs - a compared pair already agrees on the 84 routing and 33 slot key bits, so false matches cost 2^-75 per comparison, expected N^2/2^192 = 2^39.26, cap 2^44 with Chernoff tail (e mu/t)^t = 2^-5.7e13; C5 true matches, two channels - off-diagonal Poisson(0.4975) tail exp(-1.42e7) = 2^-2.0e7 at the 2^20 cap, and the diagonal challenges z = a/a' which abort at the caps with union probability 6*2^128/m = 2^-104.27 (the same single event that would break C4 and C7); C6 candidate sinks (owner candidate lists, tail 2^-3.9e6; generating-node kept-block receive, tail 2^-3.8e7); C7 re-walk key repeats (the retained key already occurs, so >= 5 kept steps need 4 further hits: L^5/(5! 2^768) per chain, 2^-451.7 over all chains); C8 node overflow (capacity 2^33.32 baby records against mean 2^31.63 per node; 2^-20 budgeted for modelling); C9 base-prime supply (Chernoff 2^-1.3e19 at delta = 1/2 under H2''). Together charged 2^-40.

Success arithmetic: 1 - e^{-K} = 0.39195 at the lower-bound K = 0.4975, minus the 2^-40 cap union, minus the 2^-20 C8 modelling budget, minus a 0.0008 census-informed allowance (the census's worst absolute toy deviation is 0.0067 at toy L, and the diagonal corrections it prices fall to zero at production L; the allowance is one eighth of that worst toy deviation) = 0.39115, claimed at 0.391 against the 0.39 required.
limitations: This is an analytic bound, not a full-size execution.
H1 and H3 are validated at toy scale only (the three coverage toys, the exact-coverage census and the end-to-end run in this package's own evidence).

Instruction counts are itemised analytic counts from an AArch64-scalar-style listing at six 64-bit limbs per field element, not hardware measurements; every shared price (the F_r-multiplication at 383, the inversion at 2^16 by the full binary extended Euclid (four six-limb values, coefficient maintenance included), the projective 4-bit-window scalar multiplication at 648 including the window table's affine normalisation, the Tonelli-Shanks square root at 2048, the modexp at 512) is derived as a worst-case bound in proof.md section 3 with its algorithm, and the cluster model is the accepted lineage's definition restated. The unit convention is the organiser's own normalisation clause: COST_MODEL.md's prices are 'rounded organizer normalization constants ... not CPU timings or exact measured instruction counts' and candidate_prices_allowed is false, so non-group work is charged as itemised instructions over the pinned 2000-instruction reference budget.

Memory is exponential, as for any BSGS-form Cheon attack: the exact integer sum is 2^122.806 bytes (the retained 2^32 x 96-byte gap table per generating node and the 40-byte linked pool records included), claimed at its ceiling 2^122.81.

The per-record charge 148 is an itemised analytic count over a 33-line six-limb listing whose maximal variant is 129/122 (a 14.7 percent margin, the same discipline as the lead's 26 percent over its listed 143, where the lead charged 180); it is not a hardware measurement. The score sits 0.0531 bits under the accepted lead and 0.0212 under the pending fork entry 116.761224; the gain is the lead's own published slack (K = 0.4975 against the lead's 0.52, charge 148 against the lead's 180 at comparable 14.7/26 percent margins) net of the honest repricing this package adds (the scalar-mul 640 -> 648 window-table normalisation); a reviewer who prices any line differently gets a different number and the ledger is a single script.
